claim: An adversarial clothing pattern optimised against visible-thermal detectors of all fusion stages at once transfers to unseen detectors better than a pattern optimised against any single detector. Supported only if the jointly optimised pattern stays above 95% attack success on every detector it was optimised against, while single-detector patterns fail on detectors of other fusion stages; and if, on four black-box detectors never used in optimisation (one per fusion stage), its average attack success is higher than that of every single-detector pattern.

experiments: Build an aligned visible-thermal 3D simulation of a clothed person and a physically realisable pattern. Setup: start from public 3D human and clothing meshes; unfold each mesh into a 2D face map and align real thermal photographs of clothing to it to give each mesh a thermal texture. Parameterise the clothing as cells that are either printed fabric (any RGB colour, thermal value of the body underneath) or aluminium film (measured fixed colour and thermal emission), never both. Render the clothed person with random physical transformations (distance, angle and so on) into aligned visible and thermal background images from FLIR-aligned (4,129 training and 1,013 test pairs; evaluation on the first 500 test pairs), and minimise the detector's confidence for the person. Optimise the mixed continuous colours and discrete fabric-or-film choices by randomly freezing 70% of cells as discrete each step and updating the others.

Fix the targets and the success measure. Setup: white-box targets covering every fusion stage: an early-fusion (Prob-E), a mid-fusion (Prob-M) and a late-fusion (Prob-L) probabilistic-ensembling detector, and separate YOLOv11 visible and thermal detectors; black-box transfer targets RPN-E, AR-CNN, RPN-L and Deformable DETR. All score clean pedestrians above 0.85 confidence. Attack success is the fraction of target pedestrians not detected at IoU 0.5 and confidence 0.6, averaged over viewing angles, distances and scenes.

Measure transfer to unseen detectors with and without ensembling across fusion stages. Setup: optimise patterns against each white-box detector alone and against all four fusion types jointly with a weighted sum of their losses; evaluate every pattern in simulation on all white-box detectors and on four black-box detectors of different fusion stages. Result: single-detector patterns transfer poorly across stages (the early-fusion pattern reaches 11.2% on late fusion and 1.0% on YOLOv11; the YOLOv11 pattern 38.2% on late fusion), while the joint pattern scores 99.8, 100.0, 99.4 and 96.2% on the white-box detectors and 94.8, 76.4, 97.4 and 99.0% on the black-box RPN-E, AR-CNN, RPN-L and Deformable DETR, a mean of 91.9% against 87.8% for the best single-detector pattern (late fusion); the early-fusion pattern is marginally better on RPN-E (95.4%).
